dependent_weighted_factorization
declarations.signature:
theorem dependent_weighted_factorization {I : Type u} [Fintype I]
    {X : I → Type v} [∀ i, Fintype (X i)]
    (weight : ∀ i, X i → ℝ) (factor : ∀ i, X i → ℝ) :
    (∑ x : ∀ i, X i, (∏ i, weight i (x i)) * (∏ i, factor i (x i))) =
      ∏ i, ∑ a, weight i a * factor i a

declarations.name: shared_weighted_contraction
declarations.signature:
theorem shared_weighted_contraction {S : Type u} [Fintype S]
    {I : Type v} [Fintype I] {X : I → Type w} [∀ i, Fintype (X i)]
    (sharedWeight : S → ℝ) (weight : ∀ i, X i → ℝ)
    (factor : S → ∀ i, X i → ℝ) :
    (∑ y : S × (∀ i, X i),
      sharedWeight y.1 * (∏ i, weight i (y.2 i)) *
        (∏ i, factor y.1 i (y.2 i))) =
      ∑ s, sharedWeight s * ∏ i, ∑ a, weight i a * factor s i a

declarations.name: splitAssignments
declarations.signature:
def splitAssignments {I : Type u} {Shared : Type v} {Internal : I → Type w}
    {Ω : Type z} :
    ((Shared ⊕ Sigma Internal) → Ω) ≃
      ((Shared → Ω) × (∀ i, Internal i → Ω))

declarations.name: vertexWeight_split
declarations.signature:
theorem vertexWeight_split {I : Type u} {Shared : Type v}
    {Internal : I → Type w} {Ω : Type z}
    [Fintype I] [Fintype Shared] [∀ i, Fintype (Internal i)]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (x : (Shared ⊕ Sigma Internal) → Ω) :
    vertexWeight μ x =
      vertexWeight μ (fun s : Shared => x (.inl s)) *
        ∏ i, vertexWeight μ (fun v : Internal i => x (.inr ⟨i, v⟩))

declarations.name: represented_port_contraction
declarations.signature:
theorem represented_port_contraction {I : Type u} {Shared : Type v}
    {Port : I → Type w} {Internal : I → Type p} {Ω : Type z}
    [Fintype I] [Fintype Shared] [∀ i, Fintype (Internal i)] [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (port : ∀ i, Port i → Shared)
    (kernel : ∀ i, (Port i → Ω) → (Internal i → Ω) → ℝ) :
    finiteDensity μ (fun x : (Shared ⊕ Sigma Internal) → Ω =>
      ∏ i, kernel i (fun p => x (.inl (port i p)))
        (fun v => x (.inr ⟨i, v⟩))) =
      finiteMean (vertexWeight μ) (fun s : Shared → Ω =>
        ∏ i, portMarginal μ kernel i (fun p => s (port i p)))

declarations.signature:
theorem finiteDensity_reindex {V : Type u} {W : Type v} {Ω : Type w}
    [Fintype V] [Fintype W] [Fintype Ω]
    (d : V ≃ W) (μ : Ω → ℝ) (factor : (W → Ω) → ℝ) :
    finiteDensity μ (fun x => factor (reindexAssignments d x)) =

declarations.name: original_carrier_port_contraction
declarations.signature:
theorem original_carrier_port_contraction {V : Type u} {I : Type v}
    {Shared : Type w} {Port : I → Type w} {Internal : I → Type w} {Ω : Type z}
    [Fintype V] [Fintype I] [Fintype Shared]
    [∀ i, Fintype (Internal i)] [Fintype Ω]
    (d : V ≃ Shared ⊕ Sigma Internal) (μ : Ω → ℝ)
    (port : ∀ i, Port i → Shared)
    (kernel : ∀ i, (Port i → Ω) → (Internal i → Ω) → ℝ) :
    finiteDensity μ (fun x : V → Ω =>
      ∏ i, kernel i (fun p => x (d.symm (.inl (port i p))))
        (fun v => x (d.symm (.inr ⟨i, v⟩)))) =
      finiteMean (vertexWeight μ) (fun s : Shared → Ω =>
        ∏ i, portMarginal μ kernel i (fun p => s (port i p)))

declarations.name: atomEdgeKernel
edge_partition_port_contraction
declarations.signature:
theorem edge_partition_port_contraction
    {V : Type u} {Edge : Type u} {I : Type v}
    {Shared : Type w} {Port : I → Type w} {Internal : I → Type w}
    {AtomEdge : I → Type w} {Slot : Type z} {Ω : Type z}
    [Fintype V] [Fintype Edge] [Fintype I] [Fintype Shared]
    [∀ i, Fintype (Internal i)] [∀ i, Fintype (AtomEdge i)] [Fintype Ω]
    (d : V ≃ Shared ⊕ Sigma Internal) (a : Edge ≃ Sigma AtomEdge)
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (U : (Slot → Ω) → ℝ)
    (port : ∀ i, Port i → Shared) (edge : Edge → Slot → V)
    (endpoint : ∀ i, AtomEdge i → Slot → Port i ⊕ Internal i)
    (endpoint_fidelity : ∀ i e k,
      d (edge (a.symm ⟨i, e⟩) k) =
        Sum.elim (fun p => Sum.inl (port i p))
          (fun v => Sum.inr ⟨i, v⟩) (endpoint i e k)) :
    finiteDensity μ (fun x : V → Ω => ∏ e, U (fun k => x (edge e k))) =
      finiteMean (vertexWeight μ) (fun s : Shared → Ω =>
        ∏ i, portMarginal μ (atomEdgeKernel U endpoint) i
          (fun p => s (port i p)))

declarations.name: privatePairMarginal
private_expansion_marginal_identity
declarations.signature:
theorem private_expansion_marginal_identity {Core : Type u} {Edge : Type v}
    {Private : Type w} {Ω : Type z}
    [Fintype Core] [Fintype Edge] [Fintype Private] [Fintype Ω]
    (μ : Ω → ℝ) (U : ((Fin 2 ⊕ Private) → Ω) → ℝ)
    (edge : Edge → Fin 2 → Core) :
    finiteDensity μ (fun x : (Core ⊕ (Sigma fun _e : Edge => Private)) → Ω =>
      ∏ e, U (Sum.elim (fun p => x (.inl (edge e p)))
        (fun v => x (.inr ⟨e, v⟩)))) =
      finiteDensity μ (fun x : Core → Ω =>
        ∏ e, privatePairMarginal μ U (fun p => x (edge e p)))

exact_question: For a finite hypergraph represented on its actual vertex/edge carriers, is its homomorphism density the shared-variable contraction of its full atom multi-port marginals?

inputs_and_conventions.sample_law: A finite sample type Ω and weights μ:Ω→ℝ. Probability interpretation requires μ≥0 and Σμ=1. The finite identities themselves hold for arbitrary real weights and kernels.
inputs_and_conventions.density: finiteDensity μ F = Σ_{x:V→Ω}(∏_{v:V}μ(x_v))F(x). All assignments are summed; injective density is not being used.
inputs_and_conventions.kernel: U:(Slot→Ω)→ℝ and edge:Edge→Slot→V are ordered-incidence data. A simple r-uniform hypergraph interpretation additionally checks |Slot|=r, each endpoint map injective, and distinct edge images. Symmetric U makes edge ordering irrelevant; none of these conditions is required for the algebraic equality.
inputs_and_conventions.port_decomposition: I indexes blocks. Shared is the actual shared-vertex carrier; Port i is its local copy in atom i with port_i:Port i→Shared. Internal i consists of that atom's exclusive actual vertices. d:V≃Shared⊕Σ_i Internal i is an explicit full original-carrier bijection.
inputs_and_conventions.edge_decomposition: a:Edge≃Σ_i AtomEdge i is an explicit actual edge partition. endpoint_fidelity checks d(edge(a⁻¹(i,e),k)) equals the local endpoint's actual joint/exclusive placement, for every i,e,k.
inputs_and_conventions.marginal: Φ_i(s)=Σ_{z:Internal i→Ω}(∏_v μ(z_v))∏_{e:AtomEdge i}U(local endpoint assignment using all port values s and internal values z).
inputs_and_conventions.conclusion: t(H,U)=Σ_{s:Shared→Ω}(∏_v μ(s_v))∏_i Φ_i(s∘port_i). Multi-port factors are retained.
inputs_and_conventions.private_expansion_specialization: Core⊕Σ_{e:Edge}Private contains each graph edge's own private vertices. With Slot=Fin2⊕Private, M_U(s)=E_z U(Sum.elim s z), exact t(J^[2+|Private|],U)=E_core ∏_e M_U(core endpoints) is proved in the candidate.

analytical_proof: Split each original assignment into its shared assignment and dependent family of internal assignments through a genuine equivalence.
Reindex independent vertex weights using finite product equivalence, then split the disjoint-sum and dependent-sigma products.
Conditional on the shared assignment, the finite sum of the product of weighted internal factors equals the product of their finite sums (Fintype.prod_sum).
Use the original edge partition equivalence and per-endpoint fidelity to transform every original edge factor into the atom's local factor. No density equality is assumed.
Normalized nonnegative vertex weights are separately proved in vertexWeight_mass and vertexWeight_nonnegative.

edge_cases.empty_atoms: Empty atom-index products equal1. Under Σμ=1 all unused vertex samples integrate to1.
edge_cases.empty_internal_carriers: Their assignment space is a singleton, so the atom marginal retains its full port kernel.
edge_cases.isolated_original_vertices: They may be included as unused Shared coordinates, even though no port references them; normalization then makes their samples contribute1. An adapter using only genuine joints must first split isolated vertices into a separate unused carrier and prove the corresponding normalized deletion identity. That deletion lemma is not separately included here.
edge_cases.empty_shared_carrier: The shared assignment is unique; density factors as the product of atom densities.
edge_cases.several_ports: The complete correlated multi-port factor is kept. No reduction to a list of independent one-root factors is made.
edge_cases.empty_sample_space: The algebra still makes sense. A normalized law cannot exist on an empty Ω, so no nonexistent probability law is asserted.
edge_cases.nonlinear_or_repeated_endpoints: Algebra remains valid for ordered incidence data. The candidate does not mistakenly infer simplicity or linearity from it.
